chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abū Bāsir, who said:

I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever dies while he is healthy and wealthy (able to afford the journey) and has not performed Hajj, he is among those of whom Allāh, Exalted and Mighty, said: "And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind."'
I said: 'Blind?' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allāh, Exalted and Mighty, made him blind from the path of truth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence for a wealthy person who neglects the obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) links the neglect of obligatory Hajj to the divine punishment of spiritual blindness, citing the Quranic verse regarding those who turn away from Allah's reminders. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that physical capability and wealth create an immediate duty, and failure to fulfill it results in a specific eschatological consequence where one is 'blinded' from the path of truth, as explained by the Imam to clarify the metaphorical nature of the blindness.
